channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone's vice presidency has produced no elected president
item.description: A public policy analyst says the office has often served party balance rather than succession, and points to Solomon Berewa's 2007 defeat as evidence.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains livelihoods as tree loss threatens land
item.description: A 65-year-old burner says his family relies on the trade, while an energy compact puts clean cooking access at just 15%.

item.title: Sierra Leone finance minister faces civil society call for dismissal
item.description: A civil society consortium wants Finance Minister Sheku Bangura removed, while a Politico SL opinion writer defends his record on inflation and borrowing.

item.title: Davids takes charge of Yanga for first league match against Polisi
item.description: The defending champions host Polisi Tanzania in Moshi after a two-week international break, with some players arriving from national-team duty.

item.title: Lusófona University awards Germano Almeida its first honorary doctorate
item.description: The Cape Verdean writer, who won the Camões Prize in 2018, is to receive the title in Mindelo on Friday at 16:00.

item.title: Eswatini unveils E1.7 billion child poverty plan
item.description: The plan targets a reduction in child poverty from 56.5% to 40% by 2028, with funding for eight deprivation dimensions.

item.title: Botswana nurses’ union urges MPs to reject new bill
item.description: BONU says the proposal risks workers’ legal safeguards and livelihoods, while the Health Ministry says it would update standards and protect public safety.

item.title: Malabo faces food inflation and power cuts as year-end demand rises
item.description: October inflation crossed the CEMAC threshold, while outages are cutting business income and making food and seasonings more expensive.

item.title: U.S. lawmaker links Eritrea trade talks to progress on peace
item.description: Representative Jim Baird's proposed Eritrea PILLAR Act would open U.S. farm exports, mining help and port access to talks once peace steps are taken.

item.title: Chad's teachers' union leader vows to press labour campaign after release
item.description: Djimoudouel Faustin, president of the Independent Teachers' Union of Chad (SIET), says he was arrested while campaigning for teachers' living and working conditions.

item.title: Njage asks court to reopen Saitoti estate distribution
item.description: The claimant says he is Saitoti’s son and wants the confirmed grant revoked, the estate’s distribution reviewed and administrators to account for its assets.

item.title: Uganda targets 500,000 metric tonnes of cocoa a year by 2036
item.description: The first national cocoa strategy also seeks $3 billion in annual export earnings and 30% local processing by 2036.

item.title: Senegal arrests former bodyguard over CFA235 million plot fraud
item.description: Investigators in Dakar say a colonel and several acquaintances paid deposits for residential land whose allocation certificates now appear to be fictitious.

item.title: Burkina Faso and Mali adopt 2027-2029 plan for shared water
item.description: The roadmap targets water-data sharing, pollution and conflict prevention, with quarterly implementation meetings planned in Mali.

item.title: Benin opens national book fair with focus on poetry
item.description: The Cotonou event runs through 22 November, bringing together book professionals from Benin, other African countries, the Caribbean and Europe.

item.title: Boko reports 51,000 reached by jobs programmes, about 16,100 permanent
item.description: Botswana’s 2026 State of the Nation Address counted public works, insourcing and other schemes, with many placements still temporary.

item.title: Angola opens gold refinery with capacity for 25 kilograms a day
item.description: The Endiama-financed plant in Viana includes a laboratory and the country’s first public office for certifying precious metals.

item.title: White Nile launches sorghum harvest as yields top 17 sacks per feddan
item.description: A Radio Tamazuj survey found sorghum selling for up to SDG 1.05 million a sack in Rabak on 16 November.

item.title: Shipena takes charge of Goeie Hoop Primary School
item.description: Appointed on 1 March 2025, Kremensia Shipena brings about 15 years in public education to the Omaheke region school.

item.title: Researchers track slaty egret to assess Okavango wetland health
item.description: The bird’s population and breeding data are expected to help authorities plan protection for its habitat in Botswana’s Delta.

item.title: Konneh seeks Senate probe of Bio Chico mining deal
item.description: The senator wants committees to examine the company's status, unpaid obligations and community commitments, then report within two weeks.

item.title: Tunisia’s oil union cancels three-day hydrocarbon transport strike
item.description: The union cited the start of workers’ social coverage regularisation and implementation of a 2019 agreement, but says other demands remain.

item.title: McDonald's vanilla cone at Rs 15 draws crowds across Mauritius
item.description: Buyers at outlets from Port-Louis to Grand-Baie are choosing the Rs 15 cone while other McDonald's desserts top Rs 100.

item.title: Shipping route changes benefit Djibouti amid Red Sea crisis
item.description: Carriers disrupted by insecurity in the Persian Gulf are reorganising routes, while the high cost of detours is drawing some back towards Suez.

item.title: Kenyan startup Dira wins US$10,000 African AI challenge
item.description: The education tool helps teachers flag learners needing attention and find tailored interventions, while keeping teachers in control of updates.

item.title: China's embassy gives N'Djamena CFA4.12 million in mosquito-control equipment
item.description: The donation, handed over on 19 November, is intended to support urban sanitation and prevention of dengue and malaria in Chad's capital.

item.title: Keur Massar investigators arrest six more men in HIV-transmission inquiry
item.description: The men were detained on 17 and 18 November after contacts on two suspects’ phones led gendarmes to new people in the case.

item.title: Ivory Coast's social security fund pushes safety committees in private schools
item.description: Only 19 of 184 eligible private schools had a committee by the end of 2025, a coverage rate of about 10%.

item.title: Liberia and Guyana sign air services deal, opening route to South America
item.description: The agreement creates a legal framework for passenger and cargo flights between the two countries, but no start date for services has been set.

item.title: Tanzania targets local processing of 30% of cashew harvest
item.description: The Cashewnut Board says domestic processors handled 27% of the crop in the 2025/2026 season, against a 60% goal by 2030.

item.title: Renamo presses parliament over water pollution inquiry in Moma and Larde
item.description: The opposition movement renewed its call for a parliamentary commission after a request filed about 14 days ago received no response.

item.title: Ivory Coast launches platform to link mining and energy projects with financiers
item.description: SIREXE Invest, launched in Abidjan, has scheduled 54 business meetings over three days in its first edition.

item.title: Namibia's banks face calls to disclose lending evidence
item.description: Black entrepreneurs say finance requirements favour businesses with wealth and established banking ties, while banks say loans are assessed by commercial risk.

item.title: Zimbabwe urged to weigh mining bill carefully before passage
item.description: The Zimbabwe Independent says the 1961 Mines and Minerals Act no longer reflects the mining industry, while mining remains important to the economy.

item.title: Orange Botswana opens Gaborone auditions for music competition
item.description: The Saturday session starts at 7am at Cresta President Hotel, with qualifying artists able to advance to coaching and quarter-finals.

item.title: House committee urges rejection of Liberia's $54.7 million identity deal
item.description: The committee found more than 40 defects in a concession that named Austrian firm OeSD as operator without a competitive bid.

item.title: Indian authorities seize 22kg of cocaine from passenger arriving from Sierra Leone
item.description: The passenger was arrested in New Delhi after officials said she posed as a diplomatic courier and presented documents linked to the United Nations.

item.title: Bensouda pledges procurement priority for women and Gambian firms
item.description: The United Coalition candidate says his government would give these businesses first preference in public contracts if he wins the December presidential election.

item.title: Mozambique's Supreme Court questions Mondlane over 2024 unrest
item.description: The former presidential candidate said his broadcasts sought support for electoral truth and justice, not destructive acts attributed to them.

item.title: Boakai to press UN Security Council on seafarer protection
item.description: Liberia plans a high-level debate on civilian crews in conflict zones when it assumes the council presidency on December 3.

item.title: Ivory Coast, Benin and Togo sign pact to study shared gas supply
item.description: The agreement, backed by the World Bank, also provides for gas exchanges between the three countries to support electricity production.

item.title: Kollie asks lawmakers to raise Cuttington funding to US$859,000
item.description: The Bong County representative’s proposal would add US$170,962 for scholarships, alongside funds for electricity and laboratory supplies.

item.title: UN mission to leave Western Sahara by 31 January 2027
item.description: The mission was created 35 years ago to organise a referendum on the territory's political future, but it will end without holding one.

item.title: Central African Republic and Chad talks stall over return of rebel leaders
item.description: Bangui and N'Djamena are negotiating the return of three rebel chiefs in Chad, but Wagner's stakes in a gold mine are among the obstacles.

item.title: Uganda tourism board backs AFCON 2027 logo to market the country
item.description: The board holds tournament marketing rights under a 30 October deal with CAF and wants fans attending in Uganda to visit beyond match days.

item.title: DR Congo plans $500 million water programme for four provinces
item.description: The second phase of the national water and sanitation programme targets 5 million people across Kongo Central, Haut-Katanga, Lualaba and a fourth province.

item.title: Malawi court to rule on bishop’s bail, with K300 million bond proposed
item.description: The State does not oppose Medram Felix Chirwa’s release if conditions are imposed, but his lawyer disputes how often he should report.

item.title: Luanar produces certified maize seed on 150 hectares for Malawi subsidy programme
item.description: The university plans to buy packaging machinery before supplying the crop to the Agriculture Ministry for distribution under the Farm Inputs Subsidy Programme.

item.title: FG suspends Lagos-Ibadan bridge work after 20-hour gridlock
item.description: The federal government halted the work following a traffic jam on the expressway that lasted 20 hours.

item.title: Malawi First renews threat of nationwide demonstrations
item.description: The group says government missed a two-week deadline to set out responses to fuel shortages, hunger, blackouts, forex scarcity and water disruptions.

item.title: Green Climate Fund approves $3.5 million for Uganda climate finance
item.description: The 48-month grant will help the finance ministry prepare projects for funding and coordinate institutions seeking climate finance.

item.title: Tinubu asks parliament to replace attempted-suicide jail terms with care
item.description: The proposal would offer medical support instead of prosecution, while a separate Senate bill on the issue has passed its second reading.

item.title: Port-Louis festival brings more than 30 food stalls to waterfront
item.description: The three-day event pairs Mauritian and international dishes with nightly music, while keeping each dish at no more than Rs 275.

item.title: Bumamuru hosts Inter Star as Burundi’s weekend fixtures begin
item.description: The teams meet at Stade Urunani at 15:00 on Friday, followed by Muzinga FC against Rukinzo FC at the same venue on Saturday.

item.title: Malawi disaster agency has 109 327MT of maize for El Niño response
item.description: Dodma says that is about a third of the 342 696MT required, as 6.5 million people face potential food insecurity.

item.title: Kenya police set December 10 recruitment at 423 centres
item.description: Applicants must meet age, education and fitness rules, and the service says applying is free.

item.title: Zambia's teaching hospital performs first microsurgical breast reconstructions
item.description: Surgeons at the University Teaching Hospitals Adult Hospital operated on two women, aged 34 and 45, who had completed breast cancer treatment.

item.title: Mbah proposes renaming ESUT after founder Jim Nwobodo
item.description: The Enugu governor says he will begin consultations and pursue the legal process needed to change the university's name.

item.title: South Sudan targets December finish for 44-kilometre Magwi–Palotaka road
item.description: Work on the Eastern Equatoria feeder road began in October under a programme linking rural infrastructure with agricultural production.

item.title: Menzo starts Kotoko reign against fourth-placed Bechem United
item.description: The new coach takes charge on Sunday with Kotoko 11th on 14 points after 11 matches in the Ghana Premier League.

item.title: Ghana's revenue authority faces GH¢680 million Safaritech judgment debt
item.description: Patrick Yaw Boamah, MP for Okaikwei Central, told Parliament the award is one of several judgment debts hanging over government.

item.title: Zimbabwe High Court orders ZIMRA to refund unlawful duty on US$130,000 car
item.description: The court ruled the returning resident met the ownership test and gave the revenue authority 30 days to calculate any refund due.

item.title: Gordon buried in Juba after November 12 ambush
item.description: The South Sudanese journalist was killed alongside Justin Akim when gunmen attacked a vehicle carrying party delegates in Mundri East County.

item.title: Danamadji sub-prefect urges farmers and herders to use legal dispute channels
item.description: Tougondjide Tedebaye Léonard raised grazing routes, poisoned fields, bush fires and relations between village chiefs and residents during a visit to Kalgoua.

item.title: Ghana targets first locally made tetanus-diphtheria vaccine by early 2027
item.description: The first of three bulk substances needed for production has arrived, while Cabinet approval is being sought for 10-year procurement agreements.

item.title: Medical charity urges wider use of Ebola vaccine in DR Congo
item.description: Médecins Sans Frontières, known as MSF, wants access to the ERVEBO vaccine expanded quickly rather than waiting for a different vaccine.

item.title: Tunisia forecasts cooler temperatures and northern rain on Friday
item.description: Highs will range from 20°C to 25°C in the north and centre, while the sea will be very rough in the north.

item.title: Iwacu imagines midterm elections holding Burundi’s leaders to account
item.description: The commentary argues that a vote between presidential elections could curb automatic second-term ambitions and give voters a way to punish unfulfilled promises.

item.title: DR Congo certifies 153.951.330,09 USD in third-quarter oil claims
item.description: The Government says it will pay the certified claims and provide fourth-quarter advances as it keeps pump prices stable amid rising world oil prices.

item.title: Madagascar streams Ambohimalaza trial as torture claims surface
item.description: The Justice Ministry is broadcasting the proceedings on social media, while allegations of confessions extracted under torture have raised concerns in court.

item.title: Malagasy debate technology's role in traditional divination
item.description: Some are adapting divination practices for apps and artificial intelligence, while others continue to use older methods.

item.title: Expert links Sampa to Facebook page in ECZ polling case
item.description: A digital forensics manager told the Lusaka Magistrate's Court that the former Matero MP ran a page alleging an illegal polling station.

item.title: Malawi opens Lundu mini-grid as developer plans 25 more
item.description: The 40 kWp solar facility in Lilongwe has connected some households and businesses, with 25 more customers registered for connection.

item.title: Ghana prepares second intake of 8,000 health workers
item.description: MP Titus Beyuo says the planned hires would follow an earlier intake and include pharmacists, nutritionists and dietitians.

item.title: Mondlane says investigation began before 2024 election
item.description: The former presidential candidate says authorities wanted to charge him with inciting a coup and block his candidacy.

item.title: Government faces questions over HELSB support for poor university students
item.description: Thousands of Zambian school-leavers pass Grade 12 and win public university places, but poverty leaves them unable to continue.

item.title: Egypt pays $38.2 billion in external debt service as reserves hit $57.5 billion
item.description: The 2025/2026 bill was $500 million lower than the previous year, even as external debt rose to $166.7 billion by June.

item.title: Egypt's meteorological authority forecasts 29°C highs in Cairo and Lower Egypt
item.description: The forecast calls for a slight temperature rise across most of the country, with morning mist and possible light drizzle in isolated areas.

item.title: Bangui beef sellers hold unsold meat as prices drive customers away
item.description: Rising supply and transport costs have pushed prices beyond many families’ means, leaving cuts on market stalls for up to two days.

item.title: Zambian commentary says president holds too much appointment power
item.description: A Lusaka Times commentary examines the extent of presidential appointment powers under the Constitution and various Acts of Parliament.

item.title: Qualcomm opens 2027 Africa startup programme to Namibian applicants
item.description: The equity-free programme offers early-stage technology businesses coaching, engineering help and intellectual-property guidance.

item.title: Guinea plans commission to prepare national airline
item.description: Transport Minister Ousmane Gaoual Diallo says the body will work with the finance ministry on plans to establish a carrier within two years.

item.title: University of Ghana questions rent laws for UGEL student hostels
item.description: The dispute follows inspections of some facilities and student complaints over charges and living conditions; four-bed rooms cost GH¢8,050 a year.

item.title: Madagascar's electoral commission seeks partners' support for 2027 elections
item.description: Thierry Rakotonarivo presented the commission's needs to diplomats and international organisations in Antananarivo, but no funding commitments were announced.

item.title: Madagascar sends Tendry to defend world pétanque shooting title
item.description: The team left for Khon Kaen, Thailand, where the championships run from 20 to 24 November and Madagascar will also contest the men's triplette title.

item.title: Nigeria cites $21 billion in oil and gas investment interest
item.description: Two non-binding memoranda cover $15 billion and $6 billion, but the investors and proposed projects have not been identified.

item.title: Bangui power cuts persist as official touts Sakaï 2 solar project
item.description: Maxime Balalou said the plant would double maximum capacity and serve 300 000 households, while outages continue across the capital.

item.title: Eswatini charges seven over Reconstruction Fund claim
item.description: Prosecutors say the claim diverted E960 000 from a fund set up to help businesses affected by the 2021 unrest.

item.title: Djibouti shows African water utilities its Doraleh desalination plant
item.description: Djibouti depends on three sources of water: boreholes, a pipeline from Ethiopia and the Doraleh seawater plant, which sends its output to the Farah Had reservoir.

item.title: SACU members seek reforms to turn revenue pool into industrial driver
item.description: An African Development Bank-backed study will examine changes to the 116-year-old Southern African Customs Union, whose transfers help fund Eswatini's public spending.

item.title: Lubombo cattle deaths top 120 as ministry helps farmers find buyers
item.description: Gall sickness killed more than 90 cattle on the Lubombo Plateau in two months, while drought and poor grazing threaten herds elsewhere.

item.title: South Africa welcomes ICJ ruling holding Myanmar responsible for genocide
item.description: The court ordered Myanmar to provide restitution and compensation to Rohingya people and guarantees that the atrocities will not be repeated.

item.title: Mali's transition council approves security inspectorate law with 119 votes
item.description: The law expands audits, evaluations and investigations across security and civil-protection services and aligns the inspectorate with the army's oversight body.

item.title: Five of eight family members die after suspected poisoning in Burundi's south
item.description: Health sources said the eight relatives were not taken to hospital until Tuesday, 17 November, days after the incident is believed to have happened.

item.title: South African cities impose water restrictions as El Niño strengthens
item.description: The US Climate Prediction Centre puts the chance of a strong-to-very-strong event through January-March 2027 above 79%.

item.title: Burundi detains more than 25 Banyamulenge refugees since October
item.description: Security services accuse the refugees of spying for Rwanda and collaborating with M23 and its allies, while families seek information about detainees.

item.title: Morocco plans SMS flood alerts backed by a 72-hour river forecast
item.description: The early-warning system would use rainfall and river-level readings to identify threatened communities before water rises.

item.title: Gambia signs agreements for 52 MWp Soma solar plant
item.description: The project pairs the solar facility with a 40.9-megawatt-hour battery system and includes a separate implementation deal with the government.

item.title: Metropolitan Health Lesotho becomes Momentum Health Lesotho
item.description: The name change followed governance, shareholder and regulatory approvals, and existing cover and contracts stay unchanged.

item.title: Ithuseng centre graduates 53 people with disabilities
item.description: The two-year Maseru programme trained graduates in carpentry, leatherwork, metalwork, and sewing and knitting.
